RFC9568-5.1.1.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 5.1.1.3 says "The TTL MUST be set to 255." TestSendAdvertV3IPv4HeaderTTLProtoDst changed only by the checksum-mode plumbing (a Checksum: packet.ChecksumRFC9568 field added to the GroupSpec, AdvertParams or packet.Local literal, or the mode argument added to packet.FillChecksum); every assertion and every isolating input is byte-for-byte the same; it still requires byte 8 of the sent frame to be 255. Single-polarity. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-5.1.1.3-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 5.1.1.3 says "A VRRP Router receiving a packet with the TTL not equal to 255 MUST discard the packet [RFC5082]." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. N4 with TTL 64 still requires ErrTTL, and TestInstanceRxDiscardsBadTTLTypeAndCountZero, unchanged, proves the discard. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-5.1.2.3-1.note: TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions/v6 reads IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS back from the tx and NA sockets and requires 255; runs only under integration && linux with CAP_NET_RAW/ADMIN, as the row's marker discloses

RFC9568-5.1.2.3-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): Same unit, IPv6: Hop Limit 255 reaches the FSM; 0, 64, 254 record exactly ttl and never reach it.

RFC9568-5.2.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 5.2.2 says "A packet with unknown type MUST be discarded." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. Type 2 still requires ErrType before the VRID lookup. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-5.2.4-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after a tag was added to TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking (body unchanged): TestOwnerAutoDetection requires EffectivePriority 255 for the owner configured at 120 and the configured 100 for a non-owner; TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking keeps the owner at 255 under any decrement

RFC9568-5.2.4-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after a tag was added to TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking (body unchanged): TestBoundaryPriority accepts 1 and 254 and rejects 0 and 255 through extractGroupSpecs/validateGroups; TestEffectivePriorityWithTracking floors a tracked decrement at 1

RFC9568-5.2.5-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 5.2.5 says "If the received count is 0, the VRRP advertisement MUST be ignored." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. The Count 0 advert still requires ErrCountZero. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-5.2.6-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 5.2.6 says "The Reserve field MUST be set to zero on transmission and ignored on reception." TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 now runs a subtest per checksum mode, and each still requires the Reserve nibble to be zero and the exact golden bytes; the receive half TestDecodeV3ReserveIgnoredOnReceive is unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-5.2.8-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 7.1 says "It MUST verify the VRRP checksum." TestDecodeVerifiesChecksumBothFamilies lost only the assertion on the removed MsgOnlyChecksum flag; it still accepts the message-only IPv4 golden and the IPv6 golden under the default mode and refuses a flipped checksum bit in each family with ErrChecksum. An overlay mutant that made the default mode sum the IPv4 pseudo-header reddened it. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-5.2.8-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after d2abad70ad). RFC 9568 Section 5.2.8 says "For the IPv4 address family, the checksum calculation only includes the VRRP message starting with the Version field and ending after the last IPv4 address (refer to Section 5.2)." Producers: pseudoSumFor returns no pseudo-header for ChecksumRFC9568, FillChecksum applies it on transmit and verifyReceived on receive in the one configured form. Positive TestEncodeGoldenV3IPv4 pins G2 0x828A (re-derived independently over the 16-octet message; the pseudo-header sum for 192.0.2.251 to 224.0.0.18 is 0xDEFB). Positive/negative TestDecodeV3IPv4ChecksumOnlyConfiguredForm: the default mode accepts G2 and refuses G2c with ErrChecksum, and each mode refuses the other form, in separate subtests, not one assertion wearing two hats. Overlay mutants run 2026-10-18 over the whole vrrp tree: restoring dual-accept in verifyReceived reds the two refusal subtests; summing the IPv4 pseudo-header under ChecksumRFC9568 reds the golden and the default accept and refuse subtests. The hop that previously made this weak is closed: doSendAdvert hard-coded to ChecksumRFC5798Compatible, or with Checksum dropped, now reds TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState, which is tagged RFC9568-7.2-5 rather than this row; the config default (groups.go struct literal) is caught only by the untagged TestLeafShapesFromTextConfig "checksum absent is rfc9568". Both are hops that choose the form, owned by the 7.2 transmit step and the parser, while this row's own obligation, what the computation covers, is pinned at its producers in both directions. Claims match assertions. No tagged unit is a QEMU-guest unit.

RFC9568-5.2.8-3.note: vrrp closure judge 2026-09-30 (independent): TestDecodeV3IPv6ChecksumCoversPseudoHeader recomputes the IPv6 golden's checksum with refChecksum (independent of checksum.go): the RFC 8200 pseudo-header plus message sum is accepted, the message-only sum is refused with ErrChecksum, so a v6 verifier that dropped the pseudo-header or fell back to message-only (as the v4 path does) goes red. Producer verifyReceived family==V6 uses pseudoSumV6 only. Both polarities recorded observed red (pseudoSumV6, verifyReceived).

RFC9568-5.2.9-1.note: TestValidateIPv6LinkLocal refuses a global-first IPv6 group and accepts a link-local-first one (transmit side); TestValidationOrder row 13 rejects a received global-first advert with ErrFirstNotLinkLocal

RFC9568-5.2.9-2.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent): the cascade confound is removed: the IPv6 group's IPv4 address now follows fe80::1, so the first-address-link-local rule cannot refuse it, and every refusal must carry the family error text ('is not an IPv6 address' / 'is not an IPv4 address'); same-family IPv4 and IPv6 lists validate. Records: revert validateGroup, both polarities.

RFC9568-6.1-1.note: TestAcceptFilterAcceptsNeighborDiscoveryBeforeAnyDrop requires ICMPv6 135 and 136 accept terms ahead of the first drop term in the Accept_Mode False table, and fails if the table has no drop

RFC9568-6.4.2-1.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: TestInstanceStartupNonOwnerGoesBackup requires a Backup to install no virtual address, the state Ze hands the kernel that answers ARP; TestInstanceOwnerStartupGoesMaster is the Active contrast

RFC9568-6.4.2-10.note: matrix row preempt-lower-priority-no-delay requires no actions (discard); preempt-false-lower-priority re-arms instead, so the discard is bound to Preempt_Mode True

RFC9568-6.4.2-2.note: TestInstanceIPv6VIPLivesOnVirtualMACDevice requires a Backup to install no IPv6 virtual address and the Active router to install it on the vMAC macvlan only

RFC9568-6.4.2-4.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Wiring now proven on the host: TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState drives the FSM and asserts the worker sets the discard on the Virtual Router MAC device at start (idle worker: on then off), entering Backup adds no call, promotion withdraws it once after the only install, and a higher-priority advert demotes and sets it again before the only removal (records observed red on doRemoveVIPs; the run revert was also observed red but the ledger keeps one record per unit/polarity). Wire effect: TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest) forwards a transit datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC without the nft drop and stops it with it (records on backupFilterTables). The host unit's negative tag is a state contrast; the violating negative (no discard, frame forwarded) is the QEMU control.

RFC9568-6.4.2-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: TestInstanceStartupNonOwnerGoesBackup requires no virtual address installed in Backup, so the kernel accepts nothing addressed to it; Active contrast installs it

RFC9568-6.4.2-6.note: TestFSMTransitionMatrix backup/shutdown requires exactly StopTimers and a transition to Initialize; the negative is a contrast row (stale timer event keeps Backup)

RFC9568-6.4.2-7.note: vrrp final judge 2026-09-29 (independent): earlier proof stands (promotion action list with StartAdvertTimer, GARP per IPv4 VIP with the Virtual Router MAC, NA per IPv6 VIP R=1 S=0 O=1 with the Virtual Router MAC). The Solicited-Node clause is now asserted at the boundary Ze owns: TestPromotionInstallsIPv6AddressesOnVirtualMACDevice requires an IPv6 Backup to install nothing, then on its own down timer to install exactly fe80::1 and 2001:db8::1 on the virtual-MAC device and never the parent; that address add is what makes Linux addrconf join each Solicited-Node group (Ze builds no MLD). Observed-red record: doInstallVIPs. Kernel membership itself is not read.

RFC9568-6.4.2-8.note: matrix row backup/advert/priority-zero requires exactly StartMasterDownTimer with skewDur; equal-priority row arms mdDur instead

RFC9568-6.4.2-9.note: matrix row backup/advert/adopt/equal-priority requires the down timer at mdDur(cfg, 4000), the recomputed interval from the advertised 4000 ms; the discard row emits no action

RFC9568-6.4.3-1.note: vrrp closure judge 2026-09-30 (independent) re-judged: the tagged units changed only by added RFC requirement tag comment lines for the new rows (8.1.2-6 / 8.2.2-8 / 8.2-4 / 8.1.1-2); test bodies byte-identical, records current, verdict unchanged. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Product install now proven: TestPromotionInstallsIPv4AddressOnVirtualMACDevice (v3 and v2 subtests) asserts a Backup installs nothing and the promoted non-owner makes exactly one install, on the virtual-MAC macvlan zv4-2-10 (never the parent), of exactly 192.0.2.1/24 (record observed red on doInstallVIPs). TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersARPWithVirtualMACOnly (QEMU guest) proves that installed state answers ARP and that no reply is seen with the address removed (records on vipCIDRs). The dataplane_linux_test sysctl tags stay without records.

RFC9568-6.4.3-10.note: matrix row master/advert/priority-zero requires SendAdvert and StartAdvertTimer; a losing non-zero advert sends without re-arming

RFC9568-6.4.3-11.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): TestInstanceIPv6ElectionUsesUnsignedOrder closes both named gaps: the IPv6 operand through the engine (link-local advertisement source) and the unsigned network-byte-order compare (fe80::80 vs fe80::7f, which a signed octet compare inverts). Yield rows assert Adver_Timer cancelled, Active_Adver_Interval set to the advert's 3000ms, Skew_Time and Active_Down_Interval recomputed from it, Active_Down_Timer armed, Backup; the hold row keeps Active, timer armed, 1000ms. With TestInstanceTieBreakComparesTheAdvertisementSource (IPv4). Records: senderWinsTieBreak, observed red.

RFC9568-6.4.3-12.note: losing lower-priority, smaller-ip and equal-ip rows require exactly one SendAdvert and state Active; the winning row demotes instead

RFC9568-6.4.3-2.note: single-polarity; TestInstanceIPv6VIPLivesOnVirtualMACDevice requires the Active router to install the IPv6 address on the vMAC macvlan, which makes the kernel join the Solicited-Node group

RFC9568-6.4.3-5.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuation 3): Wiring now proven on the host: TestBackupDiscardFollowsTheState asserts promotion withdraws the discard exactly once and only after the address install, and that it holds before promotion and after demotion (records observed red on doInstallVIPs and doRemoveVIPs). Wire effect: TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames (QEMU guest) forwards the datagram sent to the Virtual Router MAC once the filter is withdrawn and the address installed, and not while the filter holds (records on clearBackupFilter).

RFC9568-6.4.3-6.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 (independent, continuations 1-2): Re-read: the unit's body is unchanged; only the 6.4.2 and 6.4.3 Virtual Router MAC proxy tags left it for TestVRRPBackupDoesNotForwardVirtualMACFrames, so the verdict stands. Prior note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after RFC5798 tags were added to TestActiveAddressOwnerAcceptsWhateverAcceptModeSays (body unchanged): owner installs and accepts (instance and acceptfilter tests), Accept_Mode True hands no suppression, and a non-owner with Accept_Mode False gets a suppression: both conditions and the contrast are asserted

RFC9568-6.4.3-7.note: vrrp judge 2026-09-29 re-read after RFC5798 tags were added to TestActiveAddressOwnerAcceptsWhateverAcceptModeSays (body unchanged): TestActiveNonOwnerWithAcceptModeFalseSuppressesLocalDelivery requires accept=false for exactly the VIP; Accept_Mode True and owner contrasts require accept=true

RFC9568-7.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 7.1 says "It MUST verify that the VRRP version is 3." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. N9 still requires ErrVersion for a v2 advert at a v3 group. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-7.1-12.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent auditor, after 30aabfda88). Erratum 8298 (rfc/errata/rfc9568/8298.txt, Verified) corrected text: "It SHOULD verify that the local router is not the IPvX address owner (Priority = 255 (decimal)) and log the event (subject to rate-limiting) and MAY indicate via network management that a misconfiguration was detected." onPacket gained one branch before noteOwnerConflict: an owner in a group configured checksum rfc5798-compatible records ReasonOwner and returns. Every other VRRPv3 group still reaches noteOwnerConflict (owner-conflict counter on every advert, Warn log at most once per ownerConflictLogInterval) and processes the advertisement. TestInstanceV3OwnerConflictLoggedAndProcessed runs under testSpec(), whose Checksum is packet.ChecksumRFC9568, so the new branch is not taken and the test still pins the counter, the log, its rate limit and delivery; the negative (non-owner, nothing counted, no log) is unchanged. PASS at HEAD. Finding, no verdict change: in an rfc5798-compatible IPv4 group the owner now counts under `owner` and writes no log line, so this SHOULD's "log the event" is not done there (an owner-approved, mode-scoped departure toward RFC 5798 Section 7.1 as published, disclosed in docs/guide/vrrp.md). rfc/short/rfc9568.md Support remaining does not mention it and should, since the rfc-compliance rule requires an owner-approved deviation to keep its section and reason in the scope record.

RFC9568-7.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 7.1 says "It MUST verify that the VRRP packet type is 1 (ADVERTISEMENT)." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. TestValidationOrder still requires ErrType for type 2 before the VRID lookup. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-7.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 7.1 says "It MUST verify that the received packet contains the complete VRRP packet (including fixed fields and the IPvX address)." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. TestDecodeV3DiscardsIncompletePacket switched its IPv4 golden to G2 and recomputes in the default form, so the truncation and short-address cases still fail on ErrTruncated or ErrLength rather than ErrChecksum. Verdict unchanged.

RFC9568-7.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after a78870fd39). RFC 9568 Section 7.1 says "It MUST verify that the VRID is configured on the receiving interface." TestDecodeGoldenV3IPv4 now decodes the RFC 9568 message-only golden G2 under the default-mode lookup instead of the pseudo-header golden G2c, and lost only the removed MsgOnlyChecksum assertion; the subtests of TestNegativeReferenceBugs other than N1 gained only the FillChecksum mode argument. The positive is still a fully conforming advert, the checksum check precedes the checks this row names so a wrong form would fail with ErrChecksum and not pass silently, and each negative still asserts its exact sentinel. RFC9568-7.2-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after d2abad70ad). RFC 9568 Section 7.2 says "The following operations MUST be performed when transmitting a VRRP packet: ... * Compute the VRRP checksum", in the Section 5.2.8 form: message-only for IPv4, and for IPv6 "the checksum calculation also includes a prepended \"pseudo-header\", as defined in Section 8.1 of [RFC8200]." IPv4: proven, and the previous finding is fixed. Overlay mutants run 2026-10-18 over the whole vrrp tree: doSendAdvert hard-coded to ChecksumRFC5798Compatible, to ChecksumRFC9568, or with Checksum dropped, each reds TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState, which now asserts p.Checksum == spec.Checksum; encodeLocked hard-coded to either mode, or skipping FillChecksum, reds TestSendAdvertFillsFieldsAndChecksum, whose expected sums the test computes itself. Both polarities stand: the negative is the compatible-mode subtest, a separate case from the default-mode positive, and is what reds when encodeLocked ignores the mode. IPv6: unproven by any tagged unit. The kernel computes the IPv6 checksum because openV6 (backend_linux.go) sets IPV6_CHECKSUM 6; the transport unit test runs on a fake backend and its IPv6 frame carries no checksum, and the IPv6 run of TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState computes FillChecksum in the test body. Removing that setsockopt would leave every tagged test green (reasoned from the test sources: only the integration-tagged QEMU units TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions and TestIntegrationAdvertV6OnWire read it; the overlay run could not build because of another session's undefined applyVLANMTU in internal/component/iface/config_apply.go). Fix: tag one of those two units RFC9568-7.2-5 positive and take its QEMU discrimination record, which cannot be taken while the guest build fails. Claim nit: the TestTransmittedAdvertFilledFromInstanceState positive says "a default IPv4 and IPv6 group", but the test sets ChecksumRFC9568 on the spec; the parser default is proven only by the untagged TestLeafShapesFromTextConfig. Today no tagged unit of this row is a QEMU-guest unit.
